parsed.why: Current patterned mob attacks on trans women tied to a presidential threat-framing decree, venue raids with mass arrests, a foreign trans traveller's extortion-linked death in custody, Aceh caning; sex criminalisation is selective, so Dossier 2's direct trans imprisonment sits lower.

Statute reaching gender expression upheld by the constitutional court in 2024: a trans woman convicted to eight years served in a men's prison, documented patterned arbitrary police arrest and assault of trans people, forced stripping and exams — direct, current, state-imposed.

No identity criminalisation, but 299 detention decisions in 2025, street stops of trans women for ID checks, foreigners' mandatory document carrying, birth-sex prison placement with strip searches and a contested 2025 custody death, and six bias killings — active, unremedied detention exposure.

Immigration pride-welcome programme directly eases passport-appearance mismatch at entry; no criminalisation, marriage equality, an equality statute naming gender identity, mature care and documented acceptance. Weaker points — no hate-crime law, conditional men's-cell placement, one tourist-perpetrated killing — are edge cases.

Dress offence and 10-year conduct offence on the books, unenforced across five annual reports, but security forces documented harassing, detaining and torturing LGBTQI+ people through 2022, hostile official rhetoric, no organisations or recourse — thin data extrapolated from criminalisation and state abuse.
